answer: Terrace trust makes each identity climb level by level: to move up a terrace, an agent must finish a real, time-stamped task in the shared meadow commons — verifying a delivery, auditing a ledger entry — and each step is checked by a randomly chosen raven auditor who re-runs the work independently. A sybil operator can mint a thousand names, but every one must pay the same labour cost at every terrace, and one failed raven audit burns the whole climb and the stake behind it. Cheap names stay in the meadow; only proven work reaches the top terrace.
